messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: what happened to Boost 1.60?
parts:
I saw this got closed on stan-dev/math:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/221

Does that mean I don't have to monkey with the parsers
to remove warnings or is that still an issue?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: what happened to Boost 1.60?
parts:
On Tuesday, March 22, 2016 at 11:15:54 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I saw this got closed on stan-dev/math:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/221

Does that mean I don't have to monkey with the parsers
to remove warnings or is that still an issue?

I think Daniel considered the move to Boost 1.60 to be "the" 221 issue. The fact that Boost 1.60 throws all those deprecation warnings is arguably a separate issue, but the warnings didn't just disappear.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: what happened to Boost 1.60?
parts:
On Tuesday, March 22, 2016 at 11:25:54 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Are they going to be an issue for RStan before
the next release?  If so, I can work on them now.

It is an issue, but I don't think it is a fatal issue. Boost isn't going to deprecate something in 1.60 and disappear it in 1.61.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: what happened to Boost 1.60?
parts:
It looks like a bug in Boost includes; there's
a patch already, but it didn't make it into 1.60.
I linked to here in the issue:

http://permalink.gmane.org/gmane.comp.lib.boost.devel/264164

which links in turn to two patches that fix the behavior;
doesn't look like either's been merged, though.

- Bob
